posts.title: The Download: AI’s judgment problem and carbon removal’s crop threat
posts.summary: This is today’s edition of The Download, our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in the world of technology. The most misunderstood graph in AI just got a major update A new report from the AI evaluation nonprofit METR finds that some capabilities are improving exponentially—but models aren’t as good…
bullets: New data from the nonprofit METR indicates that while AI models show exponential improvement in coding, they continue to struggle with tasks requiring complex human judgment.
Anthropic’s Claude has reportedly been utilized to prove the Riemann hypothesis, a breakthrough that could fundamentally alter the landscape of mathematical research.
Emerging research suggests that enhanced rock weathering, a major carbon removal strategy backed by tech giants like Google and Microsoft, may negatively impact crop yields at scale.
The collapse of COP31 climate talks following disputes over fossil fuel mentions underscores the increasing difficulty of achieving global consensus on climate policy.

posts.title: A legendary philosopher isn’t buying Anthropic’s consciousness argument
posts.summary: This story originally appeared in The Algorithm, our weekly newsletter on AI. To get stories like this in your inbox first, sign up here. Before going public last week, Anthropic named the possibility that AI could be conscious or sentient as a risk factor for anyone investing. Given “the way we approach model sentience and moral…
bullets: Anthropic has officially identified the potential for AI consciousness as a material risk factor for investors, suggesting the company may implement stricter operational constraints than competitors.
The company's stance is rooted in the belief that as AI capabilities increase, the probability of sentience rises, necessitating a proactive approach to the 'moral significance' of AI systems.

Prominent philosopher Thomas Nagel has publicly challenged this perspective, arguing against the anthropomorphization of AI and questioning the validity of attributing subjective experience to non-biological systems.

The debate highlights a growing tension between AI safety ethics and corporate governance, as Anthropic's philosophical commitments could lead to significant competitive disadvantages or regulatory hurdles.

posts.title: Why using rocks for carbon removal could eventually reduce crop growth
posts.summary: Tech companies are investing a lot of hope and money in rocks. Google, Microsoft, and others have committed hundreds of millions of dollars to get startups to spread crushed basalt, olivine, or other alkaline materials across farms, in an effort to capture carbon from the air and lock it away. A number of influential models…
bullets: New research from CarbonPlan indicates that the carbon removal potential of enhanced rock weathering (ERW) may be significantly lower than the previously estimated 3 to 8 billion metric tons annually.
The study reveals a critical trade-off: excessive application of alkaline rock to farmland to capture carbon may eventually suppress crop yields, threatening agricultural productivity.
If application rates are limited to protect soil health, the total carbon sequestration capacity of ERW could be capped at less than one billion tons per year.
The findings introduce significant financial and operational risk for tech companies that have invested hundreds of millions of dollars into scaling ERW as a primary climate mitigation strategy.

posts.title: Hybrid-Bonded 3D NAND Boosts Analog In-Memory Compute Density (IBM, Micron, U. of Patras)
posts.summary:
Researchers at IBM Research, Micron Technology, and University of Patras published “3D-NAND-CIM: A Hybrid-Bonded 3D-NAND-Flash-based Analog In-Memory-Compute macro offering 4.8M weights/mm².” Find the technical paper here. November 2026. Pritish Narayanan, Athanasios Vasilopoulos, Geoffrey W. Burr et al. “3D-NAND-CIM: A Hybrid-Bonded 3D-NAND-Flash-based Analog In-Memory-Compute macro offering 4.8M weights/mm².” arXiv:2611.27479, November 20, 2026. https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27479.
The post Hybrid-Bonded 3D NAND Boosts Analog In-Memory Compute Density (IBM, Micron, U. of Patras) appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Researchers from IBM, Micron, and the University of Patras have developed a 3D-NAND-based analog in-memory compute (CIM) macro achieving a density of 4.8 million weights per square millimeter.
The project utilizes hybrid bonding technology to integrate high-density 3D NAND flash with analog compute capabilities, significantly enhancing efficiency for AI workloads.
This advancement demonstrates a viable path for scaling memory-centric computing architectures, potentially addressing the memory wall bottleneck in large-scale AI model inference.

posts.title: Measuring Verification Gaps In LLM-Generated Post-Quantum Hardware (Lucid, EYL)
posts.summary:
Researchers at Lucid Motors and EYL Inc. published “From FIPS to FPGA with LLM Agents: Measuring What Tests and Reviews Miss in Post-Quantum Cryptographic Hardware.” Abstract “As LLM agents increasingly generate RTL alongside the tests and reviews that validate it, self-generated evidence is a weak foundation for trustworthy hardware. We present our seven-stage verification-gated workflow,... » read more
The post Measuring Verification Gaps In LLM-Generated Post-Quantum Hardware (Lucid, EYL) appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Researchers at Lucid Motors and EYL found that LLM-generated hardware verification often overstates reliability, with standard simulation gates failing to catch 24% of tool-selected netlist mutants.
The study introduces a seven-stage verification-gated workflow that emphasizes author-independent mutants and formal checks to ensure the security of post-quantum cryptographic hardware.

The findings suggest that while LLMs can accelerate RTL development, they require rigorous, human-audited verification frameworks to prevent critical security flaws in sensitive applications like key-custody cards.
